hypothesis: Aggregating 4 independent RAG-drafted sets should surface decision-critical unknowns (they recur) and suppress niche/redundant ones (they don't), giving a new criticality signal that beats single-sample RAG.
technique: Four independent exp003-style RAG calls at temperatures [0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0] produce 28 candidate questions; all 28 are embedding-clustered (NLEmbedding cosine, merge threshold ≥ 0.62) in Swift, and the 7 clusters with the broadest cross-sample agreement are kept, each represented by its centroid-nearest member.
